text_fidelity_a:
OHDERII TV Projector I got excited to see one of these small portable LED style ones that actually had a decent native resolution (most of them can accept 1080p, but are in reality only 800x600 resolution, or sometimes worse... 640x480!). This one is actually capable of displaying 720p of real dot resolution, which should make it at least as sharp as my Viewsonic and other traditional HD projectors. Ok, perhaps I'm spoiled, but I'm comparing this to our Viewsonic 720p projector that, to be fair cost me 3-4x as much.
And for the most part, it DOES work, however there are some caveats to its use. First of all, it doesn't seem as sharp as my 720p projector, even though it should have the requisite amount of dots. It's OK, its definitely better than the cheap 600p projectors, but something just isn't quite there when comparing side by side. It also doesn't get all that bright, but I suppose that's expected from the LED tech being used. You'll need black out shades or use it only during the night. Then there's the color- it isn't great. It works, but it has a cheap color reproduction that looks kind of flat and lifeless. Dark scenes sort of all blend together and become nearly impossible to see. It lacks the vibrancy of even an inexpensive television from decades ago. It gets the job done, but hardly the "theater experience" if you've been waiting to see that latest action/vfx film the way it was intended. It will look better on your TV at home, the only thing this has going for it is the large projection experience. For example, if you just want to give your kids a backyard movie night and don't care that the color and detail won't be as great as your indoor system, it will do the job on the cheap. I personally would not give up my mid-range projector for this one.
One thing that I found particularly annoying is that rather than the optical zoom and focus dials found on usual projectors, there is only a focus and tilt dial. No zoom. That means you have to physically move the projector closer or further to get it to reach the correct size you are shooting for. That actually got in the way of using it in a couple of specific places my other projectors can be used at optimal sizes.
That's not to say it gets everything wrong- I DO like that it is small and light and can even be turned on it's back to aim at the ceiling. That's something my big projector can't do, due to the airflow and cable management sticking out the rear. It also has a standard 1/4" 20 threaded tripod mounting point, so you can place this onto a tripod and get maximum mounting freedom. That will come in handy as I've always wanted to watch a movie in bed on the ceiling. But otherwise, don't think this projector will be as good as the other mid-rangers out there. This is still very much a low end projector. You'll have to spend at least 2-3x as much to get a decent home theater style experience, and much more if you want a high end one that will handle FHD/4k to get the real deal. This is more of a specialty use item.
text_fidelity_b: OHDERII TV Projector

text_fidelity_a:
Nyne Boost Waterproof Portable Bluetooth Speakers with Premium Stereo Sound - IP67 Water & Dust Proof, 20 Hours Play-time, 100 ft Range, Built-in Power Bank and Mic, Loud Wireless Speaker,Grey Having outdoor safe speakers is essential for my household. Not only do I have audiophiles who are addicted to headphones and speakers, I have a husband who insists on taking his speakers to outdoor jobs. that is fine except when the job turns out to have a sudden rainstorm or high dust going on. Before giving it to him, I had our daughter put it through the grind at work (food prep) and in town events. Let's see how this speaker performs..

WHAT IS THIS SPEAKER LIKE?
This speaker is gray in color. The housing is very rubbery in consistency. The right side of the speaker has sealed controls under a rubberized pad over top of the buttons. The speaker stays put and is heavier than expected.

ON/OFF BUTTON/PAIRING
Holding down for over a second powers up the speaker. Next to the power button is the PAIRING button. This is not for pairing the speaker to a device but it is for pairing with another speaker just like it. A coworker with my daughter has this speaker and they tested it out- works GREAT so you now get two synced speakers.

CALLS BUTTON
You can send and receive calls with this button. You can also access your voice commands on your phone with this button.

VOLUME BUTTON
This is plus or minus sound controls. You can also skip by holding down- + is forward, - is backward.

PAUSE/PLAY
You can control pausing and playing with this button.

DOCKING
USB for charging, mini USB port (to use to charge a device if need be), and auxiliary outlet for like an old MP3 player or other device that does not have Bluetooth capability.

CHARGING INDICATOR LIGHT
Red when charging and turns white when fully charged. Will indicate when the power is running low so you will know.

SOUND QUALITY
Sound quality with this is very good. My daughter has a coworker with the same speaker so they both have had a chance to experiment with their speakers. So far it has been a great speaker. The balance of the recording of course affects the speaker, but so far it has not been overly muffled, out of balance, etc. Where you put the speaker affects how it sounds too.

When put on the floor, it really does sound better than on, say top of a box, or couch, etc. A very hard surface seems to really make it sound best.

VOLUME
When using the volume controls on the speaker, the sound is better than when you use the volume controls on the device (tablet, phone, etc).

DURABILITY
This speaker was taken to a huge town chicken and biscuit dinner and was dropped and still is working perfectly.

BATTERY
Two 10 hour shifts at full volume, and this speaker kicked through it all before needing to be recharged.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a really nice durable speaker that is dustproof, shock proof, and supposedly water proof, this is a good choice. It is solid, has decent sound , and even can be synced with another speaker if you get two of these for coverage around a room.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a decent speaker, and I feel more comfortable having my husband use this on his jobs than the other really nice speaker he was beating up.
text_fidelity_b: Nyne Boost Waterproof Portable Bluetooth Speakers with Premium Stereo Sound - IP67 Water & Dust Proof, 20 Hours Play-time, 100 ft Range, Built-in Power Bank and Mic, Loud Wireless Speaker,Grey

I agree with others who have said the cover is a bit pricey, but if you love your Kindle Touch as much as I love mine, you will want to protect it for many years to come with this sturdy jacket.

text_fidelity_a:
AMD FX 4100 4-Core Processor, 3.6 4 Socket AM3+ FD4100WMGUSBX My old computer was exactly that: Old! It needed some serious work. I was running an Athlon X2 6000+ and an EVGA 9800GT. It was a great system back in the day! But, time took its toll. I was kicking around the idea of getting an Intel i3, since they seem to edge out this chip, and are competitively priced (I never overclock my equipment, so it's at stock settings.) But the future upgradability seemed like it'd be very costly. Over all, this chip performs just fine. I mainly upgraded so I could play Diablo 3, and with an EVGA 550 Ti, I play it on high settings, and it looks as good as I could want it to look. My old machine did just fine with standard productivity stuff, but I wanted to play games that were more recent than WoW. I'm able to do everything I want, with no signs of a lag. If I need to upgrade, I'm banking that the next generation of this chip will see some improvements (though the improvement I'm seeing from my last CPU is leaps-and bounds!) The AM3+ socket will be around for a while. Over all, this is a great chip, and easy on the wallet.

**Update 9/6/12**
I recently purchased Guild Wars 2. The game is fairly CPU-intensive, but the FX-4100 keeps up just fine! I think I'm sitting at around 50% plus load at any given time during actual game play on all four cores. I haven't had a single hiccup or spot of lag yet!

Starcraft 2 is another CPU-heavy application, and coupled with the 550 Ti card, I'm running it on Extreme at 1400x900 resolution, and it's flawless. Again, all four cores are loaded, and quite frequently, they're over 60%. Things get a little warm (35C or so) when compared to when I run other applications. Nothing to worry about!

I have also paid quite a bit of attention to how it runs with Diablo 3. It only uses 2 cores at about 50% load at any given time. That game is more GPU-intensive. I am still very happy with my purchase!
text_fidelity_b: AMD FX 4100 4-Core Processor, 3.6 4 Socket AM3+  FD4100WMGUSBX

ARRIS SURFboard SB8200 DOCSIS 3.1 Cable Modem | Approved for Comcast Xfinity, Cox, Charter Spectrum, & more | Two 1 Gbps Ports | 1 Gbps Max Internet Speeds | 4 OFDM Channels | 2 Year Warranty,White I replaced a large bulky router/modem combo from my ISP with this modem, as I already had a good router and didn't need two routers. My ISP was charging roughly $10 a month for their equipment, which I will save now. Of course the SB8200 is a little bit pricey, so it will take me about one and half years to recover my cost. I was surprised how small this modem is; very compact and easy to find space for. It generates a little heat, but has vent holes all over the outside and top for good ventilation. Most of heat come out the top, but obviously you don't want to block any of the openings and make sure there is plenty of space above it. I am getting great speed from the modem and had no issues with it at all. My ISP was able to set it up remotely in about 30 minutes. All the "experts" say it is best to have your own equipment, rather than rent from an ISP. I like that idea, but the only problem is that if equipment fails, you are responsible for it, whereas if you rent from the ISP, they replace any defective equipment at no cost. Also if you need an equipment upgrade, the ISP covers that too. I don't expect to need an upgrade as this will handle the fastest speeds being offered now by my ISP (1 Gbps), although not yet in my area. Right now I have 300 Mbps and the modem handles it nicely without any problem. This modem does NOT use the Puma chipset, which was causing some issues. This is a great
piece of equipment and suitable for home or business. Just has 4 lights (power on, upload, download and connected to internet). I thought I had seen comments about the lights being dim, but they are nice and bright; maybe bright enough to almost be distracting at times. Am very happy so far with the modem and would buy one again if it lasts well over time. There are a couple other modems by other quality manufacturers that are somewhat comparable to this one, but in side by side comparisons this seems to rate a little better. The Arris brand was recommended to me and it is the brand used by my ISP.
text_fidelity_b: ARRIS SURFboard SB8200 DOCSIS 3.1 Cable Modem | Approved for Comcast Xfinity, Cox, Charter Spectrum, & more | Two 1 Gbps Ports | 1 Gbps Max Internet Speeds | 4 OFDM Channels | 2 Year Warranty,White

text_fidelity_a:
OTTERBOX DEFENDER SERIES Case for iPad mini (5th Gen ONLY) - Retail Packaging - BLACK So. Yes. It’s sturdy and seems it’ll protect an iPad really well.

Unfortunately, for the past 6 years, we’ve been spoiled by an iPad mini case made by Ballistic, that isn’t made any more. So I just don’t buy “well sure it’s inconvenient and bulky but it has to be, to protect well.” It really does not.

This plastic Otterbox uses is so very rigid, the protective cover is extremely difficult to pop on and off. When kiddo’s alarm goes off and he’s already off somewhere, it takes me ages to get the thing open to shut it down. I also can’t find the power or volume buttons easily by touch, they blend in so much.

What’s outright laughable is the kickstand. It’s on the inside of the cover that you take off, so you set the iPad on it. It doesn’t sit very securely at all, and now that this model has the pencil holder, in some positions it won’t stay up - it teeter totters right over! So no, it’s not a 4 position kickstand, but a 3 position. The whole situation is anything but stable, so if there’s a tug on a charger or headphone cord, instead of just sliding a tiny bit on the table or not doing anything at all, it slips off the kickstand and ... well, this is how we already know it’s sturdy, as the thing ended up on the floor more times in the first day than the iPad did in a year in its old case.

It’s quite heavy compared to other choices that offer similar protection, and very very difficult to install. I am never need to read directions type, and these directions were meaningless. It required a YouTube and a lot of swearing, plus a sliced open cuticle, to get it on. Even then it didn’t seat properly around the speakers and needed quite a bit of poking into place with a toothpick.

I sincerely hope there will be a day when there’s another rugged iPad mini case, with a kickstand and a shell that goes over the screen. Because this just doesn’t cut it.
text_fidelity_b: OTTERBOX DEFENDER SERIES Case for iPad mini (5th Gen ONLY) - Retail Packaging - BLACK

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin vívoactive HR GPS Smart Watch, Regular fit - Black My in-depth review of the new Garmin Vivoactive HR that debuted this week ($249/AMZN) and that I've been wearing since Saturday is as follows:
-- It buzzes and vibrates a lot. Not sure what it's doing because by the time I look the message has disappeared.
-- I ran with it and managed to stop it at 1.46 miles and don't know how I did that. Had to restart another run. I should be able to figure this out in about 3-4 months.
-- It is counting my steps for some reason and I really don't care how many steps I take. My goal is to take as few steps as possible to get where I need to go, especially if where I need to go is the bathroom
-- It's waterproof and can be used in the pool for lap swimming, yet I've still taken it off each time when I shower. I don't know why.
-- It has a green light under it that's tracking my HR at all times. When I was running it showed my HR was elevated. This was not suprising in any way, considering I usually look like I'm in the midst of an anuerism when I run, even if it's just to the bathroom.
-- It is "tracking" my sleep. I found the little screen that showed my HR while I was asleep and or/if I was "deep sleeping" or if I had any movement. Unless it can help me remember what I was dreaming about, or at least stop dreaming about being back in High School with no pants, I plan on taking the watch off when I sleep.
-- I was able to sync it to my phone and put the Garmin Connect App on my phone. Both are legitimate milestone events for me. Now whenever I get a text message on my phone my wrist buzzes and my phone beeps. The writing on the phone is small and I can't see it without my glasses, so I don't need this, especially since my phone has to be close by for the bluetooth to even work. This seems redundant and at some point I'll figure out how to stop this.
-- Other things it shows are the weather (again, it's on my phone which is 2 feet away), and "intensity minutes". I don't know what Intensity Minutes are, but I'm wondering if that would include me stressing out looking for my keys each morning or trying to convince my child that she needs a shower.
-- It's impossible to see the screen in the dark. I run in the dark. Now I need to bring a light to see how far I've run in the dark.
-- The app for my phone for Garmin has all sorts of things on it as well, mostly the same things we see on the watch, but with loads more information such as circles, graphs, and lines. It continuously tells me that it's not synching with my watch, but my watch has the little BT symbol showing, so I think it's purposely pi#‪#‎ing‬ me off to add on some Intensity Minutes.
Overall, it's black and tells the time. If I remember to wear it and start it when I run, it'll tell me how long it took to do my runs and how far I went, which was never really that important to me in the first place.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin vívoactive HR GPS Smart Watch, Regular fit - Black

text_fidelity_a: Swimbuds Sport Premium Waterproof Headphones & 11 eartips in 4 Styles (Upgraded Cord) This is my second pair of Swimbuds. I've always struggled finding headphones that would not leak while swimming.  It must be some anatomical issue with my ear canal, because I've tried at least a dozen headphones - and all of them leaked or fell out at some point.  These swim buds are so light that they actually stay in my ear.  Short cord doesn't get tangled up.  And I guess the Christmas-tree tips are a bit different because so far these headphones are the only one that have not leaked, but I do have to insert them deep into ear canal.  I use just a touch of petroleum jelly on tips to help the insertion and to moisturise ears, because these headphones (like most other waterproof headphones) can cause irritation of the external ear canal.  There are a lot of tips to choose from. text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 700 Rechargeable Remote with Color Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Let me start, we are a family of dedicated logitech-harmony remote users for the over 7 years. We love the easy of set up and allowing you to out in a large number of electrical devices onto one remote.

So we decided to try this one for our bedroom devices and we were somewhat disappointed with the limitations on this model:

1. when using the harmony software there were a lot of limitations when compared with the 900 (and previous models). The limitations included:
a> couldnt change the order of the activities. ie if you want dvd ahead of music, you would not do that. To over come this: you need to preplan the order at which the devices are set up. In the more expensive models and in previous older models, you could set everything up and then re-order them.

b. once you are in a device: it only offers you four functions on the face, instead of 6 to eight. to overcome this you need to scroll to another page.

c. the device has four hard buttons to operate only four devices. Hence this remote is not useful if you have a decent home theatre. okay for a bedroom with a TV, tivo, dvd and music system.

Typical features of the device: all the button light up in the dark, except for the four device buttons and the help button (so you need to learn where they are on the remote). A good thing about this device (we also have the 900) is that the bottom half of the device have a very similar layout so no learning where the volume, channel button are placed.

The software is similar to other harmony remote, but once you indicate which remote you have: the choices are very limited.

It is worth buying the 900 and above for living room devices; and if you could find the 880, its former model, get it as the functionalities are much better. And yes, the software will support this older model. Buy the 700 if it is only for a couple of applicances. However, if you are a harmony user, you will feel a little frustrated with the limitations of this model.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 700 Rechargeable Remote with Color Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Lexar JumpDrive S47 128GB USB 3.1 Flash Drive (LJDS47-128ABBKNA) I have had a need for an additional storage solution for my laptop which will enable me to back up files, and transfer between desktop (my workstation) and my laptop when necessary. My goal is to have it as an alternative mini hard drive, so to speak. Let's take a Look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a tiny Jumpdrive, for those who have never used one, it is similar in appearance to a dongle that you use for wireless keyboard or mouse in the USB port. It does not have a case and the packaging is rather difficult to open.

WHAT IS THIS FOR?
This is designed not to carry with you all of the time like some of the flash drives, but to use almost as a mini hard drive and keep it in your laptop or even desktop if desired. It will keep your files handy, has a pretty fast transfer rate, and has a decent amount of storage, depending on what kind of files you plan to store on it.

WHAT ELSE CAN YOU USE THESE FOR?
This can also be theoretically used to keep in the car as a way to play music on your sound system via USB port. I have not been able to do that yet as I have had some issues setting up the right format. I am not sure how security will interact with that..

DOES THIS HAVE SECURITY ON IT?
This drive has a program called ENCDataVault Lite. That will allow you to encrypt your files and have them accessed with a password you set up in case you lose your drive at least your files will be somewhat protected unless it is a hacker who finds it.

HOW IS TRANSFER RATE?
I have used this in a USB3.0 as well as USB2.0 port and both worked well.

DOES THIS FIT TYPE C CONNECTION?
You can not use this in a type C port so please check your laptop or desktop prior to purchase to be sure you have an actual USB port to use this in that is not already being used.

WHAT I DON'T LIKE ABOUT THIS
This drive should come with a tiny case on a keychain or with at least a loop handle on it so that you can put it somewhere safe and not lose it. It does not come with that. Something this small needs to have a colorful case to make it harder to lose. I know that the idea is to have it stay in the unit you use it on mostly, but sometimes you have to take it out and it needs a case.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a tiny drive. It is meant to use in either a car sound system (USB port), on a laptop or desktop that you plan to use it on regularly, and not be moved around constantly. It does not come with any kind of case at all to store it in when not in a port. It does have encryption which is a big plus to theoretically protect files in case of loss.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. The performance is top notch. The fact that this does not come with a case is worth removing a star. Ideally it would not be a problem most of the time, but I still think that it needs protective COLORFUl case for those times you need to remove it from a port and take it from one place to another.
text_fidelity_b: Lexar JumpDrive S47 128GB USB 3.1 Flash Drive (LJDS47-128ABBKNA)

text_fidelity_a:
MOOLINK WiFi Digital Photo Frame, 1920 * 1200 Full HD Display, 1080P Digital Picture Frame, 10.1 inch Touch Screen, 16GB Storage, Share Photos via App or Email, Smart WiFi Electronic Picture Frame I love technology, but I can't navigate new tech as easily as I used to. I fear that I'm turning into my parents, who needed my help with programming the VCR. These days, everything seems to have software that you must navigate, and it is seldom as intuitive as it once was for me.

This frame was easy to figure out, though, at least for the features I care about. I skipped right over the parts where it wanted to connect to my network and so forth. I just wanted to upload photos from a micro-SD card, and then have it play them back to me. And it does that very well.

It has a light sensor that adjusts the brightness of the screen automatically if you enable it to, which is a very nice feature that is lacking on my other digital picture frames. I was also able to program it to go to sleep when I'm never up, to save on energy. I didn't want it to be motion activated, as I want it to be displaying photos the moment I walk into the room. Fortunately, this feature is already off by default.

The frame looks really nice, with a small "mat" border around the display. This mat is something that most digital frames are lacking, and let me tell you, this tiny feature makes a huge difference. It really sells the idea that this is a picture frame, instead of merely a digital display. I can't say enough about how much this improves the aesthetic of this frame.

I have a couple of digital frames that I use in a horizontal orientation, so I deleted all my vertical photos from them and moved them onto this one instead, and set it up in a vertical orientation. It is so nice to have the frame matched to the orientation of the photos! You don't get those huge bars on the sides or top/bottom, or if you have it set to crop then you don't crop out 2/3 of the photo!

I have no complaints about this digital photo frame. I can't speak for all of the features, because I have no use for some of them. But the features I wanted work great, and the frame itself looks fantastic!
text_fidelity_b: MOOLINK WiFi Digital Photo Frame, 1920 * 1200 Full HD Display, 1080P Digital Picture Frame, 10.1 inch Touch Screen, 16GB Storage, Share Photos via App or Email, Smart WiFi Electronic Picture Frame

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon AF-S DX NIKKOR 55-300mm f/4.5-5.6G ED Vibration Reduction Zoom Lens with Auto Focus for Nikon DSLR Cameras This is my current go-to lens. I wish I could afford one of the more fancy-schmancy professional telephotos, but until then, this one is the one parked on my Nikon D7000.

Uses:

1. Birds, bugs and other critters from a safe distance or on the fly/run
2. Portraits of one or two people (gives excellent bokeh)
3. Landscapes and seascapes, especially in vertical/portrait mode.

Limitations:

1. Buildings from across-the-street distance
2. Large groups of people
3. Macro shots from thisclose

Depending on the type of photography you enjoy, this may or may not be the lens for you. It works fine for me for the uses above, especially when the subjects are a respectable distance away, but it doesn't have a wide enough angle for limitations 1 and 2, and if you're closer than a couple of feet it won't focus properly.

It's also pretty heavy, but makes up for this by making you look like a pro who knows what they're about, especially when you use the lens hood (included and highly recommended for use)

The auto-focus is not as smooth as it should be, and you can sometimes hear the mechanism moving around trying to do its job, but image stabilization and the tripod detection mode are huge pluses. (It also attaches/detaches from the camera in the opposite direction to my other (Sigma) lens)

For the type of photography I'm doing at the moment. even if it's not on the camera, this lens goes with me wherever I roam.

Amanda Richards, March 30, 2012
text_fidelity_b: Nikon AF-S DX NIKKOR 55-300mm f/4.5-5.6G ED Vibration Reduction Zoom Lens with Auto Focus for Nikon DSLR Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
Sony UBP-X800 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Player Picture is nice,

The real reason I'm sending the units (I've had two) back, however, is that the player refuses to output the various high quality audio formats, including 7.1 DTS Master Audio. The digital coax cable barely works and the HDMI 2 audio output simply does not work, Admittedly I have an older receiver -- a Sony STR-DA5400ES, from 2009. But it has multiple HDMI inputs and the HDMI 2 audio output on the X800 is specifically designed to send audio to an older amp. Even Sony phone support says it should work. But it doesn't.. I spent 1 hour and 7 minutes with Sony ES support today going through every possible menu permutation on both the Amp and the UBP-X800 player. No luck The HDMI is dead. Zero output. The coax output can only send DTS EX 5.1, even though the player itself tells me it's playing DTS Master Audio 7.1.

This UBP-X800 has two HDMI outputs: one for video, one for audio. In case you don't have a 4K receiver with the ever-changing HDMI protocols, you're supposed to be able to feed HDMI audio to the amp. So I fed the video directly to the Samsung's video input (a direct cable connection) and another HDMI to my amp.

Zero audio from the player's HDMI audio feed. Not a peep of audio at all.

So I used the orange RCA digital audio coax connector to get surround sound audio.

But the coax digital audio cable only delivers DTS EX 5.1, not the 7.1 DTS Master Audio available on the Kingsman 4K disk. I updated the player's and the TV's firmware and read the manual. Nothing fixes the problem. Using all new, very short, high-speed HDMI 2.0 cables too.

My ancient Sony BDP-S560 Blu-ray player feeds all formats to the same 5400ES amp properly. I get great 7.1 DTS Master HD audio. Thus my old Blu-ray player sounds way better than my brand new advanced Sony UHD player.
Researching at the Sony forum under the UBP-X800 Audio Problems thread, answers were all over the place and none worked, I tried to register so I could post my problem and the website wouldn't allow me to. The comments there were complaining that they could not get the ATMOS tracks working.

I have no choice but to pack both X800s up and send them back.

Eventually I found that I needed to plug the 4K player into input 3 of the TV for the image to stabilize. Interesting that only some inputs on the TV can handle UHD source. But still, the player's audio doesn't work with my Sony Amp (Sony's fault).

HDMI was supposed to solve all these problems, but I suspect the HDCP copy protection schemes are really screwing things up or the firmware has bugs or companies just produce inferior products. Rather disappointing.
text_fidelity_b: Sony UBP-X800 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Player

text_fidelity_a:
RALENO 2 Packs LED Video Light and 75inches Stand Lighting Kit, CRI 95+ Photography Lighting with 8000mAh Built-in Battery & LCD Display, Studio Lights for TikTok, YouTube, Live Streaming, Videography I ordered the 'RALENO LED Video Lighting Kits With 75inch Light Stand, 1 Durable Handbag And 2-Pack 384 LED Soft Video Light, Built-in Lithium Battery 3200K-6500K Video Lighting Kits For YouTube Photography Shooting' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts.

I ordered this kit to add more lighting options to my photography gear. My first impressions were that this kit is pretty complete in the sense that you get two lights with A/C power cords, stands for both lights, two shoe mounts and a decent carry case. With that said, I was not so impressed with overall quality of all included items. However, for all that you get in this kit, I am still quite impressed. Although this kit isn't of the best build quality it most definitely has great value with all that is included. The lights themselves are smaller than I had expected and the highest brightness setting isn't as bright as I hoped, yet it still has a place, and has come in handy many times to ad a bit more lighting to some of my projects.

I love that it includes the soft case and that the lights themselves have screens on the back that will actually show the color temperatures as well as the brightness level. I have more expensive lights that just have knobs on the back to adjust these settings with no easy way to know what color temperature you are at. This in-of-itself is a huge bonus as far as I am concerned. With this set I an easily select the exact color temp for each light to match. The stands are pretty basic. They are lightweight and easy to set up and take down. I am not so impressed with the quality of the Hot Shoe adapters as they are hard to solidly tighten the angle down without feeling like I am going to break the plastic knobs. They do function however, and I do appreciate that they included these, otherwise you would not be able to adjust the angle of the lights. The soft carrying case is decent and does have some padding if you don't throw out the included foam inserts.

Overall I find this kit to be effective, and have found that even though I may criticize many aspects of it, I do find myself using it quite often because of how convenient and easy to use and set up. There is most definitely value to this kit and I think that it would make a great lighting starter kit as well as a kit to ad more lighting options to your current lights. I hope that this was helpful.
text_fidelity_b: RALENO 2 Packs LED Video Light and 75inches Stand Lighting Kit, CRI 95+ Photography Lighting with 8000mAh Built-in Battery & LCD Display, Studio Lights for TikTok, YouTube, Live Streaming, Videography

iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey Last year I switched to a Macbook Pro 13-inch after being a PC user since the early eighties. I love my Mac, but I haven't gone whole-hog for the rest of the pricey iProducts Apple puts out. Still, this case is just about perfect for my needs.

First, I like how the zippered compartment for the computer does not unzip all around. It's really easy to slip my Mac in and out of its fleecy padded pocket while still feeling like it's protected. (There's also plenty of room for my little wireless mouse dongle, although I don't use a mouse much anymore.) The iPad compartment is similar, and it holds my Kindle Fire in its rooCase with room to spare for something else (like a checkbook or wallet perhaps). The clever half-case compartment with pockets for chargers, headphones, and pens has plenty of room for my Mac power supply, Kindle charger and cables, and another charger if I need it.

The full compartment in the middle of the case is for whatever you might stick in it. It's not huge in depth, but it would certainly hold a legal pad/portfolio and a magazine or two. I don't use a cell phone now, but one day I might, so the outer pocket for the phone is nice; it's also serviceable for one of those small flashlights or perhaps a set of keys (on the right keychain). Toothbrush! I could see using the sleeve as a lapdesk/laptop stand while seated on a plane or in a doctor's office.

The sleeve comes with a classy, comfortable shoulder strap with strong, reliable clips. At first it wasn't clear what the the clips were supposed to clip to, but they are hidden away under the edges of the center gusset (what you see as the narrow black line running across the thickness in the photo here). There's no tangling up with this shoulder strap, either; the business ends can be rotated to keep the strap straight.

It's lightweight. And the color? It's a perfect match for the Mac Lion startup screen, of course. Everything about it says "Mac," including the iHome logo, but you don't have to be an Apple nut to love this sleeve. Very well designed.
text_fidelity_b: iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey

Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black Fortunately I bought this at a much cheaper price at $16 instead of the current price as of this writing at $27. There are lots of comparable wireless vertical ergonomic mice less than $27 that also include recharging and cool LED lights. Although it's a decent ergonomic vertical mouse, there are some legitimate gripes with this mouse after months of use so now I'm looking to try a different brand of vertical mouse.

The 2.4Ghz range is pretty bad. I found this out later down the road when I had to switch the USB dongle to a port on the back of my computer. At first I thought my batteries were low (or some dirt interfering with optical sensor) because my mouse cursor would stagger on and off as a moved cursor across screen. That was really frustrating not only for browsing but games. When I put the dongle closer to the front of computer it worked much better.

Now onto the batteries. This may be good or bad depending on preference but it uses AAA batteries. Although replacing batteries seems like an inconvenience, if you have a mouse with a built-in rechargeable lithium ion battery and the batteries go bad or defective then you would have to trash the whole mouse instead of just replacing the batteries.

There is a separate top button on the mouse for DPI toggle (800/1200/1600) but I can't tell what mode it is in unless I move the mouse across the screen every time I toggle it so it is kind of inconvenient. Would be nice so you can visually see the dpi on the mouse or on screen.

Overall, the mouse feel good upon touching it. The texture on the mouse is not glossy plastic but has a slight comfy texture on it. My personal gripe with the ergonomics is it feels a bit narrow and the hand does not feel relaxed. I think the culprit is the thumb rest position feels like it is a bit upwards causes your thumb to squeeze inward instead of relaxing. So I try not to point or put my thumb in the default thumb rest but more below the thumb rest or even slight bend my thumb so it's not straight and stiff.
text_fidelity_b: Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Compressed Air Duster, Electronic Air Duster, Portable 40000 RPM Cordless Dust Blower, 6000mAh Battery Air Can Duster, Powerful Computer Keyboard Cleaning Air Spray, Rechargeable Electric Canned Air This air blower is simplistic with no added bells or whistles, but wow is it super powerful! When you push the button you can really feel your hand move from the power of those 40,000 RPMs.
I started using it right out of the box, as it came already charged. It only took seconds to blow out my tower PC. It did such a great job I actually went around blowing the dust off of everything, from the back of the TVs, the tops of all my door frames, and the shelves in my laundry room and pantry until the battery ran out, which was only around 15 minutes.
One of the best things is, is that the charger actually plugs into a wall outlet. There's no USB cord to keep up with and no searching around for an extra brick, which is never included with devices these days. It does take between 2 to 2.5 hours to charge the air blower to only get about 17 minutes of use out of it. For your typical electronic dusting and such, that's a good amount of time, but if you're wanting to use it for dusting other things, that's not long at all.
Overall, this is one powerful beast of an air blower and works great for electronics and regular dusting needs. The low usage time per charge leaves quick work of any of the other advertised uses for this device. Even with that, I still believe this air blower deserves at least 4.5 Stars ✨ and I definitely recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Compressed Air Duster, Electronic Air Duster, Portable 40000 RPM Cordless Dust Blower, 6000mAh Battery Air Can Duster, Powerful Computer Keyboard Cleaning Air Spray, Rechargeable Electric Canned Air

TRENDnet Wireless AC1750 Dual Band Gigabit Router with USB 3.0 Share Port, Pre-Encrypted, TEW-812DRU Let me preface this review by explaining that I work in the IT industry and support a variety of businesses with enough thorough experience in networking to say with certainty - the router I received is absolute garbage.

Now, normally I'd say for this price that you should set you expectations quite low - being in the field I'm in, I understand that almost all consumer routers are not great options, and the ones that are somewhat viable are on the $300+ range. Not everybody has the money or cares enough to invest this much - I get that.

So, that leaves me and my old roommate pretty much one option; the TRENDnet Wireless AC1750. He doesn't need much and especially doesn't want to spend much, it was tough getting him to go high enough in price to even this router- the old router he had came with his cable subscription 3 years ago. It worked fine but was sometimes slow with downloading over WiFi, not surprising. From the research and reviews, and most importantly the price - we decided to try this Trendnet AC1750 router.

WOW what garbage - he no longer gets WiFi in his bathroom corner of the house - it is a VERY small 2 bedroom apartment. How in the world can this router not handle a signal from 20 feet away, with only 2 walls in between? A router of this caliber (even at this price) should EASILY be able to handle covering a 2 bedroom small apartment. Period.

On to the second problem - even if we're connected, the WiFi signal drops constantly, I have to now reset this router every single day by unplugging it and plugging it back in because it refuses to work longer than 16 hours before crapping out. I have tried updating firmware, all network resets I can. I've even tried using the old modem (we replaced both router + modem) to see if that was the root of our problems - nope, it's the router.

It has slowly been getting worse and worse, and when I am gone from this apartment my roommate will be forced to reset his router every day, sometimes twice a day, just to get internet - or purchase a new one.

I am extremely dissatisfied with this product, although not quite surprised or disappointed given its price. It just seems odd that a 3 year old Netgear N300 router performs much better than an AC1750 Dual Band router.
text_fidelity_b: TRENDnet Wireless AC1750 Dual Band Gigabit Router with USB 3.0 Share Port, Pre-Encrypted, TEW-812DRU

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Keyboard, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers I had decided I did not "need" a Kindle, having tons of other gadgets for all sorts of things. Then I began to lose the vision in one eye and realized over a period of weeks that I could not read normally (or at all some days). Magazines, books, the newspaper.... heck even email was difficult to impossible some days. All my friends have Kindles, so I borrowed one for a day and fell in love. We immediately ordered the Special Offers Wi-Fi Keyboard version. I've had it about 45 days now and my quality of life has seriously improved! I can enlarge the font and change the style of the font depending on my needs at that moment and on really bad days, when my eyes are tired or refusing to focus, the voice function is amazing. The very idea that it reads aloud to me is tremendous and once you adjust to the sometimes robotic pronounciation of some words, it works like a charm. So far, all the books I've purchased have allowed the voice option.

I signed up for Audible.com about two weeks after getting the Kindle and the quality of the audio books on my Kindle is excellent. No robotic voice here - you get the narration exactly as read by the real person - it's an MP3 file I think. Additionally, getting the local newspaper every morning on my Kindle has returned to me my morning tradition of the local editorials & coffee. I do love the number of free books available as well - some are garbage, but most are pretty decent and some have been excellent books. (Loads of Sc-Fi for free too, what's not to love?) I have used the sample option for a ton of books and it's helped me decide to spend the money purchasing a novel, or not. In case you are worried about the Special Offers... they are the screensavers while the Kindle is in sleep mode and NEVER show up in your actual books. I've used a couple of them already now that I think about it.

One last thing - the Kindle in a case, fits into almost all of my handbags and has saved my sanity sitting in doctor's office waiting rooms and at the car repair shop, and I can now sit out under a tree on a pretty day with my horses again while I read a great book. This version of the Kindle will also play my own music while I'm reading. Bottom line is that the Kindle has helped me get a valuable part of my life back and this in turn has allowed me to be more rational while facing possible permanent loss of vision in one eye. Very worthwhile purchase!
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Keyboard, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver) I recently purchased this to replace a lost remote for a piece of high end integrated amp. As with most things in the audiophile world, a replacement for this simple 6 button remote was way overpriced ($105) for what it is. So I was pleased to find that my amplifier was supported by the Logitech 650.

My biggest gripe is nearly a dealbreaker. After setting it up I went to use it on my integrated amplifier to raise the volume a little bit. The problem was that I couldn't just give the volume button a quick tap to turn up the volume a little bit. A quick tap of the volume raised the volume a significant amount whereas the original amp controller allowed me to make volume changes in small increments. After some searching I found that I just had to adjust the IR repeat length in the controller setup.

Problem solved, right? Wrong.

First issue was the manual being outdated. The frustration started when I tried following the steps in the manual. The first step was "Click Troubleshoot at the top of the Harmony Remote Software window". The problem was that there was no Troubleshoot button anymore. They had updated the software but didn't update the manual. Eventually I found the new location in the software where you can lower the repeats. The default was set to 1 so I lowered it to 0 (the lowest setting on the 0-4 scale). I saved my changes and after waiting for the remote to update I tried it again and it still was making large volume changes. With the remote already set to the lowest setting the only way I can make small adjustments to volume is to press the volume button and cover the IR emitter on the remote extremely fast so the volume change signal only gets sent out for a quick burst. I'm talking ninja fast. This is extremely annoying and tricky to get the hang of.

PROS
-Price
-Device Compatibility

CONS
-Can't make small volume changes
-Outdated Manual (they updated the software but didn't update the PDF manual with new instructions for the new software). This causes some serious frustration when you are instructed in Step 1 to press a Troubleshooting button that no longer exists.

Final thoughts... I bought this to mainly do one thing. Change volume and input selection on my integrated amp. The inability to change the volume in small increments is a constant annoyance. It should be something that can be fixed with a software or firmware update.

Logitech, please fix this on the software/firmware side.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
HP 8100 Desktop Computer Intel i5 3.2GHz Processor 8GB Memory 1TB HDD Genuine Windows 10 Professional (Renewed) I wanted to wait and use it a while before leaving a review.

First off, it is larger than I expected it to be. That's okay - just had to rearrange everything.
Secondly, it is a refurb, so there are limits as to what to expect. My old computer had a hard drive die.
I got a new hard drive, but for some reason, it would never connect to the internet again after that.
I downloaded new drivers, etc etc, but nothing. So, couldn't really go without any longer, so looked for a refurb.

I like sticking with HP because I've used them for years. I've even had refurbs.
This one is different.
First of all, it lays horizontally instead of like the towers I've always had.
It looks a little rough, but not unreasonable.

it grunts at me while using it, much like my old dying hard drive did, so that does worry me a little bit.
It sounds like a grumpy old man who doesn't want to get out of his chair to reach the remote.
There are plenty of USB ports on this one. It lacks some things I'd like to have, but hey...

My biggest complaint is the lack of RAM memory on this. It only came with a measly 8GB.
That might sound okay, but it isn't. Everything moves in slow-motion. Copying files is a nightmare.
I can't afford to buy more memory right now, so I have to just suck it up.
We raided a couple of my other computers which are all HP, but of course, NONE of the six memory sticks I had
will fit this one. *bang head on desk*
The speakers are HORRIBLE. If you have ears, you'll want to replace them or add your own.
I do have speakers, but have not yet hooked them up, because it has to be done on the back, and I have to move
a lot of stuff to pull it back out enough.

This also has Win10, which I dislike a great deal. Seems like everything was moved to a new place just because they could.
But I'll deal with that. Most of the time, I can ignore the Win10 junk.

Overall, it will do what I hired it for, which was to get me back on the internet.
But if you work with graphics (like I do), know that the lack of memory will be sand in your shorts.
Everything takes much longer than on my old HP tower.
text_fidelity_b: HP 8100 Desktop Computer Intel i5 3.2GHz Processor 8GB Memory 1TB HDD Genuine Windows 10 Professional (Renewed)

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG X5 Portable SSD - 2TB - Thunderbolt 3 External SSD (MU-PB2T0B/AM) Gray/Red Samsung X5 External SSD Thunderbolt 3 (500 GB)
This drive is marketed as the fastest External SSD currently on the market. From my testing they are not overstating that claim. I was able to transfer 250Gig of data (using a 2016 MacBook Pro) to the Samsung X5 drive in just over 7 minutes.

The drive uses a magnesium alloy (rather than aluminum) for this case. This means that the drive will not throw off as much heat. Due to this fact the drive has thermal management which will slow the drive down (after extended use) to keep it from over heating. Just be aware of this should you need to move very large files back and forth.

Pros
- Very fast transfer rates
- Comes with Thunderbolt 3 cable
- Solid build quality

Cons
- Expensive. The T5 version is only $109.00 [hence the one star drop. If a tad less expensive, we would have given it the full five stars.]
- Drive may slow down when continually transferring large files due to thermal management.
- Only works with Thunderbolt 3 ports.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG X5 Portable SSD - 2TB - Thunderbolt 3 External SSD (MU-PB2T0B/AM) Gray/Red

text_fidelity_a:
Zinwell ZAT-970A Digital to Analog TV Converter Box (for Antenna Use) We needed to save some money, and I'd heard that Over The Air broadcasts included channels you wouldn't otherwise get. My Dish TV account provided local channels and a whole bunch of channels I didn't use; but the OTA feature really helps!

I paired the Zinwell digital / analog converter box (highly rated, outstanding Amazon price) with the Radio Shack Antennacraft® HDX1000 Amplified HDTV Antenna (also highly rated). You should know one thing -- the mast size for the Dish TV is larger than the mast size for the Antennacraft antenna, so you can't just remove the Dish and replace it with the Antennacraft on the same mast. But it is an easy install.

As a trial, before going up to the roof (2 story house), I set the Antennacraft in the downstairs window that has a view to the southwest (the direction our local TV stations broadcast from). Without the Zinwell, you're limited to the low power analog stations (mostly Spanish language, a few home shopping stations). I think I got about 6 stations. Then I plugged in the Zinwell in line between the antenna and the TV (after disconnecting the Dish TV feed), did a scan, and had 20 channels. Repeated the process upstairs (remember, we have a 2 story) and had 22 channels!! All the local tv stations (NBC, ABC, CW, ION, PBS, etc.) that broadcast digitally came through great!! Unfortunately, it started raining :( so after the rain stopped, I only got as far as getting the mast installed outdoors before it got too dark. It won't take long to finish.

Only one Zinwell related item: You're supposed to be able to choose the feed from the Zinwell to the TV to be either Coax or the Composite (yellow video, red and white audio). I couldn't get the composite to work in setup, but the coax worked just fine. Haven't had a chance to see if, once programmed, the composite would work, or if for some reason I hooked it up to my tv incorrectly (hard to imagine), but ... since the coax works so well, and video and audio quality are great, I'm money ahead and not complaining!!

So when do I break even? $80 antenna plus 2 $40 boxes = $160; Dish TV was costing me about $55/month (yeah, once you've been a subscriber for a while, there's essentially no customer retention policy, so, good by Dish!! -- and that's probably true for Directv and Comcast, too). So after 3 months, essentially at the start of January, I'm home free!! Thanks, Amazon, you're helping me save money, and that's really great!!

NOTE: I only ordered one Zinwell to test out things, now I've ordered a second for our other TV (didn't want to put too much at risk if it didn't work, but it works great!).

NOTE 2: The gov't coupon program is long dead, no hope of getting $40 off on one, just be glad if you waited that these things are as reasonably priced as they are.
text_fidelity_b: Zinwell ZAT-970A Digital to Analog TV Converter Box (for Antenna Use)

Bad

Future
1. I wish all profiles were directly linked to actual accounts...regardless of house hold...make it truly personalized. Signing into an account should be step one of adding a new profile.
2. I hope they go a tad bigger 15" is nice but maybe something in the 20's

text_fidelity_a: SkipDr DVD and CD Manual Disc Repair System, Single I was a little nervous about this product given the mixed reviews. It comes with the machine, a solution, and a rubbing cloth.  My daughters favorite Disney movie was scratched and skipping a lot so I wanted to fix it.  I wet the cd with the solution and placed it in the machine.  The machine has to be set on a hard flat service. I tried to just hold it in the air and it would not work. I made one round and then reapplied the solution, then cranked the machine around again.  (It goes slowly). I buffed the DVD with the cloth as directed and played the DVD. It skipped less than before, but was still skipping.  I repeated the entire process again, and now the DVD works perfectly!.  I want to try this on some very scratched  DVDs and see how far I can push it. I would recommend this for mild to moderately scratched DVDs/ CDs at this point.  Remember it says it is very important to keep the disc wet with the solution the entire time and rub it throughly with the cloth or it will not work, so do not skip those steps.
text_fidelity_b: SkipDr DVD and CD Manual Disc Repair System, Single

SereneLife Battery Grass Cutter, Grass Clippers Cordless, Trimmer Cutter, Handheld Trimmer, Grass Shear Electric, Perfect for Leaves & Debris, Rechargeable Battery, Charge Time 4 Hrs, 3.6V I really wanted to like this product, but it just didn't work out.

First of all, you need to have a really good, smooth, white surface (preferably a dedicated movie screen) to achieve the optimum results. A very, very dark room would also help. Yes, of course you could use the wall, a bed sheet or some other improvised backdrop, but it would defeat the whole point of seeing a film in the manner this projector was designed for.

Also, you must put up a credit card in order to use any of the channels available to you. Even if you are only accessing the free channels. And between you and me, I'm not that excited watching the NASA channel nonstop. You could use your Prime membership to watch movies, but that wasn't so great either.

Other reviewers have suggested it would be terrific for a slumber party. Really? What's the matter with your big screen T.V.? The picture quality is excellent but the sound is not up to par. If you're gonna go this far then you really need to be firing on all cylinders with the sound and the picture.

In conclusion, this is really a disappointment. I had hoped I could watch baseball or something else of interest to me, but this projector requires too many variables to line up perfectly, and it's just not worth the time or the effort.

The one positive - it's really cute and small.
text_fidelity_b: SereneLife Battery Grass Cutter, Grass Clippers Cordless, Trimmer Cutter, Handheld Trimmer, Grass Shear Electric, Perfect for Leaves & Debris, Rechargeable Battery, Charge Time 4 Hrs, 3.6V

Charges batteries quickly, but only 2 at a time. Still, I charged 4 batt. in an hour, as opposed to 4 in 4 hr with the similarly priced ENERGIZER. 2. Power Strip with USB 6 AC Outlets 2 USB A & 1 PD 18W USB C Fast Charging 6.6ft Desktop Extension Cord Flat Plug Wall Mount for Home Dorm Room Travel Office Accessories (Black) (Black) I originally got this to put on the other side of our headboard so that our hidden outlet is more accessible once I put up our new storage shelves in the bedroom.

HOW THIS COMES
This came in a box. It has basic information in it.

CORD
The cord is actually 6.6 ft long. I needed the extra length for the place I had set aside for it.

LAYOUT
The layout of this outlet strip is excellent I can put any type of plug in there and it works. The USB cords are also laid out well.

PERFORMANCE
I found this to be excellent. It has a small footprint on it so does not take up much space. I side mounted it on the side of our headboard on my husband's side of the bed. It is nice to be able to recharge things or have USB cords handy as well as electrical outlets.

LIGHT
Unfortunately after I put it up, I remembered that there was that bright red light on the switch. In a bedroom that is a problem so I took it out of there. Our other side has a similar outlet strip without a light on it so I did not give it a thought like I should have.

WHAT I USE IT FOR NOW
I use this as a wall mount to plug in my aquarium pumps, lights, etc. into. The small footprint makes it great to use.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice compact little outlet strip/box. It is set up well and works well. It does have a light on it, though, so if planning to use in a bedroom keep that in mind.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a great unit. I am going to get this when my UPS units finally fail in my sewing room so that I can have a small outlet to use out of the way instead of the big UPS one that has given me issues anyway.

It is USB 3.0 compatible, and worked fine on a USB 3.0 port on a Win 7 machine. It also worked just as well (albeit slower) on a USB 2.0 port on a Win 7 and an XP machine. Simple plug and play, with no drivers needed. It comes with a USB cable.

The reader is compact, measuring just under 3.5 inches long and about 1.75 inches wide. It's very low profile, standing about ½ inch tall. The card slots are on the front, and the USB connection is on the back.

Simple, straightforward and works well. That's pretty much all I need in a card reader. Hopefully it will last longer than my previous one - I'll update the review should this not perform well over time.

Telescopes for Adults Astronomy - 700x90mm AZ Astronomical Professional Refractor Telescope for Kids Beginners Astronomy with Advanced Eyepieces, Cool Christmas Astronomy Gift for Men, White I use the 'refractor' telescope as a long-range spotting scope. The 90mm aperture is the step up from a 50 or 70mm spotting scope.

The larger the aperture (objective lens), the more light enters. The amount of light captured by the 90mm aperture is a 'reflector' mirror comparable to a 114mm 'reflector' telescope, which is the other 'next step up' option for stargazing. However, 'reflectors' are higher maintenance (mirror cleaning and stability), sensitive to temperature, and more sophisticated to operate and collimate. An avid astronomy hobbyist must ultimately step up to the greater magnification, higher-quality optical path, and more expensive 'reflector.' For spotting wildlife & birdwatching, the 90mm refractor is ideal.

The 700mm focal length is comparatively short. To calculate the magnification, divide the focal length by the aperture. 700mm/90mm = 7.8 better known as f/7.8. For comparison, a 1000mm focal length, typical with a 90mm aperture, is a significantly more powerful f/11.1. But, tube length is important for remaining concealed in spotting scope mode, which is my specific interest. The 700mm length works well in a confined stand.

This refractor type is simple to operate. Assemble it, and you're in business. Plus, the magnified image is right-side up. This telescope is about as easy to set up as I've seen.

The scope comes with an above-average stand. Unfortunately, the horizontal plane locking screw mechanism is insufficient to secure the tube weight in horizontal spotting mode. The fix is easy. The telescope tube employs the fix in its lens eyepiece adapter.

Foreign objects are visible in the main eyepiece. However, the eyepiece internal optical path appears to be inaccessible.

By comparison, this 700x90 scope seems overpriced for the quality.

One month later: I replaced the artifact encumbered 25mm eyepiece with a 32mm Plössl eyepiece. Huge improvement in eye relief, full broadband multilayer coatings, and a whopping 50° increase in FOV.
text_fidelity_b: Telescopes for Adults Astronomy - 700x90mm AZ Astronomical Professional Refractor Telescope for Kids Beginners Astronomy with Advanced Eyepieces, Cool Christmas Astronomy Gift for Men, White

3.7V 30W(peak) Portable Bluetooth Speakers with Double Subwoofer Rich Bass, Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Speaker Support FM Radio, Small Stereo Sound System for Home, Party, Outdoor Travel(No Light) I have tested and reviewed literally hundreds of Bluetooth speakers and while I am not a fan of music that is particularly bass heavy I found this speaker produces rich, vibrant sounds from all wave lengths. It produces more than ample volume for most any setting and has several connection methods.

While I have tested and reviewed Bluetooth speakers costing ten times (and more) what this does, the sound quality from this speaker is really quite good. In relation to the sound quality I would place them on par with mid to high end Bluetooth speakers.

In regards to charging time and battery life, both are outstanding. In my tests charging takes about approximately 2 hours to charge the built in 4000 mAh battery and the speaker lasts a solid 4.5 hours at max volume - 8 hour with volume midway (of course this will vary a bit due to exact settings).

There are multiple ways to connect to this speaker including Bluetooth 5.0, which can reach much further than previous versions, through an AUX cable, a 3.5mm jack, TF card, USB flash drive, or FM radio - it even has a built in extendable antenna.

While it has a remote and I tested it and it works fine, I rarely use it as I connect with my phone all the time.

I have taken this speaker with me to the pool for the last couple of months and have been thoroughly impressed with its performance. The battery, being 4000 mAh, is much longer lasting than most allowing for all day listening and the sound quality has been really good.

This is an all around great Bluetooth speaker that I certainly recommend.

The professional reviews I'd read before I received it set my expectations pretty low by saying it's a nice device for the price, but the reality is that it's just a really nice device!

I have an iPad (first generation..., so no camera), and I like it, but I'm not a power iPad user. I use it to stream movies, read, surf the internet, and play games. The Kindle Fire does all of those things, but has the added bonus of being more portable, which is a pretty big deal to me. My iPad has always been a home device for me because it's too big to realistically throw in my purse. The Fire is the perfect size for portability! However, it is still significantly larger than a smartphone, so I can read or watch movies without squinting or holding a device up to my face.

One big weakness it does have - the E-Ink on the other Kindle models is far easier on the eyes when doing heavy reading. I'm hanging on to my Kindle 3 for that reason. The kind of reading I'll be doing on my Fire is more along the lines of magazine reading, looking at recipes, newspaper articles, stuff like that.

Overall, the Fire is a solid purchase. If you're thinking about buying it, just do it. You won't be disappointed!
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

text_fidelity_a: SABRENT USB 3.0 Tool Free Enclosure for 2.5” and 3.5” Internal SATA Hard Drives (EC-KSL3) I was all set to return this because it would not recognize my Seagate 4TB SSHD. In disk management it showed up as GPT protective partition. After googling, I found that the only way to get past this was to use Diskpart and Clean the drive--that meant wiping out everything on the drive. Since I had already cloned it, I went ahead and used the Clean command and wiped it out. Still couldn't do anything with the drive in disk management. So using Diskpart again, I used the command, Create Partition Primary. At this point, Diskpart couldn't do anything else. It would not create a volume to format, so I had to use Disk Management to create the volume and format it to exFat. I should state that the drive was recognized by my computer internally when it was connected to a Sata port, but once it was put into the Sabrent, it's drive information was changed and made unusable until I performed the procedure above. Not sure why this happened, maybe because it's a SSHD, but I kinda doubt it since I had no problems with the drive when connected to a Sata Port.
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT USB 3.0 Tool Free Enclosure for 2.5” and 3.5” Internal SATA Hard Drives (EC-KSL3)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony HT-A5000 5.1.2ch Dolby Atmos Sound Bar Surround Sound Home Theater with DTS:X and 360 Spatial Sound Mapping, works with Alexa and Google Assistant,Black This arrived well packaged and without issues. I've tried out several major brand soundbars in recent years, and I've yet to find any that are as good as the Sonys, at least as a television speaker. I've already got an A7000 that I'm familiar with to compare this A5000 with. It's a step down in price and feature set, but there's more to the differences than that.

The A7000 has cloth speaker covers on top, while this A5000 has plastic. It's my impression that the sound is a bit better out of the cloth, since it provides less of a reflective barrier, but it's also hard to keep clean and safe. Being on top of the speaker facing up, it's right where something can get pur or dropped on it, or a cat walking across it. The hard plastic seems much more resilient. It's also hard to tell on the sound, because the A5000 has two fewer speakers.

The top of this speaker is a textured plastic, like a car's dashboard. Not super fancy, but resilient. The A7000 has very shiny black plastic, which looks very nice and is easy to clean, but also lacks resilience and shows dust more readily.

The remote is infrared, so you need to have line of sight to the speaker for it to work, but it's full featured, even having buttons to control optional additional speakers. which I really appreciate.

The instruction book is pretty good. Setup is easy, especially if you connect it to a television. It'll put the menus right up on the screen. It's really built to be a television speaker with bluetooth and other inputs so it can be used for other things as a secondary purpose.

I'm still trying to figure out what I can do with the Chromecast feature that seems to be present in the speaker, but not in the television. So far I haven't had much luck connecting with Chromecast.

I definitely like the A7000 better, but there's a solid price difference. I love having a second HDMI input, since the way they've got these things set up, it outputs to my Sony television rather than the other way around, so I need to plug in extra devices to the soundbar, not the television, which makes it a weird decision to put so many more ports on the television than the speaker.

Great speaker, but still plenty of things that could be improved in a future version, like more satellite speaker compatibility, some kind of port passthrough from television, chromecast video, etc.
text_fidelity_b: Sony HT-A5000 5.1.2ch Dolby Atmos Sound Bar Surround Sound Home Theater with DTS:X and 360 Spatial Sound Mapping, works with Alexa and Google Assistant,Black

Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter This seemed to be the perfect solution to a problem I was having with obtaining Internet access in my basement. The router is located on the upper floor of the house and, while access is fine in every room above ground, access in the basement has been minimal at best.

Installation was very straightforward - just plug one adapter into the router, the other into the wall socket, and plug in whatever device needs access into one of the three plugs located on the wall socket device.

Overall it works pretty well, but is highly sensitive to noise or heavy draws on the power line. For example, I have a dehumidifier in the basement. When that kicks on, I lose the connection. Sometimes it is regained all by itself, but most of the time I have to either reboot (or power cycle) the device that is plugged in, or unplug and then re-plug the adapter. I tried moving the dehumidifier to a different circuit than the one used by the powerline adapter, and also tried plugging the dehumidifier into a surge protector - no difference. So, I make sure the dehumidifier is off before I use any Internet device.

I've had the same issue with other appliances such as certain vacuums - turn them on, and the connection is lost. There have been no problems with appliances operating in other areas of the house, such as the microwave, laser printers, etc. Just happens when you use the appliance in the same room as the powerline adapter.

But, other than these powerline induced interruptions, the device works well. Speedy connection - can't tell any difference between this and any other WiFi connected device. Well worth taking a look at if you have some WiFi dead zones in your house. Just keep an eye out for someone who is about to use a vacuum when you're at a critical spot in the movie you're streaming!
text_fidelity_b: Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter

text_fidelity_a: WD 8TB My Book Desktop External Hard Drive, USB 3.0, External HDD with Password Protection and Backup Software - WDBBGB0080HBK-NESN Buyers should note that this drive is formatted in exFAT. Without knowing this, I plugged it in to a running computer and began to transfer some files. The computer was shut down for the night. The next morning, I found that the computer refused to boot up with the new drive installed. Unplugged the drive, and the computer booted up fine. Finally checked the file system. Found it to be exFAT. Moved the files off and re-formatted the drive to NTFS and the problem went away. I suggest anyone purchasing this unit just save yourself the time and trouble and reformat it right out of the box. The software on the drive isn't needed anyway. I have several Western Digital external drives and this is the first one that arrived in a format other than NTFS.
